summary.text: Morgan Griffith is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election to a ninth term representing Virginia's 9th District. A Salem attorney who spent 17 years in the Virginia House of Delegates, including as House Majority Leader, he was first elected to Congress in 2010. He serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, where he chairs the Health Subcommittee.

paragraphs.text: Born in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, in 1958; his family moved to Salem, Virginia, when he was an infant, and he graduated from Salem's Andrew Lewis High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree in history from Emory & Henry College in 1980, graduating with honors, and a J.D. from the Washington and Lee University School of Law in 1983.
Returned to Southwest Virginia after law school and practiced law for nearly three decades.
Served in the Virginia House of Delegates from 1994 to 2011, representing the 8th District; was elected House Majority Leader in 2000, the first Republican in Virginia history to hold that position.
Won the 9th District seat in November 2010, defeating Democratic Rep. Rick Boucher, who had held it for 28 years.

Serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee: chaired its Oversight and Investigations Subcommittee in the 118th Congress, chaired the Environment Subcommittee at the start of the 119th Congress, and is now chairman of the Health Subcommittee.
Also serves on the Committee on House Administration and, per his office's biography, is Vice Chairman of the Committee on Rules, to which Speaker Johnson appointed him in the 119th Congress.

Told Cardinal News that the work he is most proud of in Congress is fighting the fentanyl epidemic, including passage of the bipartisan Drug Quality and Security Act on compounding pharmacies, and that a current priority is the Rural Obstetrics Readiness Act on maternal health.
According to his official biography, he is married to Hilary and they have three children.

sources.title: Griffith seeks a ninth term in the 9th District. This time, he faces a cattle farmer from Bedford County.
